equity_bridge.note: ¥102,243m at 30 Sept 2026 (cross-shareholdings at fair value + equity-method affiliates); their dividend/equity income sits outside operating profit and is not in the flows (matching-asset rule). 20% haircut for deferred tax on unrealised gains and unlisted-stake illiquidity.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (14.7%) diverges >30% from equity (5.0%) and revenue (4.4%) CAGRs because the FY2021 base (year ended Mar 2021) was COVID-depressed (EPS ¥91.92 vs ¥128-142 in the prior three years). On a FY2020 base EPS growth is ~6%/yr. Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computable: FY2026 owner FCF is negative (-¥35.3bn) on Accelerate 2028 capex, versus +¥13.2bn (FY2021) and +¥15.1bn (FY2023). Owner FCF = reported FCF here (no SBC disclosed; interest income not stripped as the company is a net borrower). Equity CAGR is depressed by ~¥100bn of buybacks over five years; revenue 5yr CAGR selected as the through-cycle anchor, with year 1 driven by the revised guidance rather than the CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Year 1 lands slightly under the revised ¥1,491bn / ¥123bn OP guidance as the H1 pre-emptive-demand pull-forward partly reverses in H2. Growth then settles at 3-4% for two years (plan mostly but not fully delivered, no M&A credited) and fades to 1.5% as the domestic housing and infrastructure businesses track Japan's demographics while HPP (interlayer film, electronic materials) and renovation/infrastructure renewal grow mid-single digits. EBITDA margin matures at 13.0% with D&A at 5.0%, i.e. OP margin ~8%, below the 9.4% plan target. The Accelerate 2028 capex programme depresses owner FCF to roughly zero in year 1 and only reaches a mature ~5% FCF margin from year 6, which is why the valuation is terminal-heavy and why the capex normalisation assumption matters more than the growth path.
scenario_narratives.bull: Accelerate 2028 delivered: ¥1,600bn+ sales and ¥150bn OP by FY2029 on sustained semiconductor/display strength, HUD interlayer film and aircraft demand, housing mix-shift to apartments and high-end homes, and a successful SOLAFIL perovskite ramp (100MW line FY2028 in repo labels). Margin reaches 14.2% EBITDA and growth fades more slowly (2% terminal with 1.5% perpetuity).
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 FY2027 beat was substantially front-loaded demand; H2 reverses, FY2028 is flat, and the HPP cycle turns while Middle East raw-material inflation squeezes spreads. Housing new-build volumes keep falling. Margins revert to the 11-11.5% EBITDA range of FY2021-FY2023, the committed capex earns sub-par returns, and restructuring/impairment charges keep recurring. Terminal cap 13x, growth 0.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on a diversified, modestly cyclical Japanese industrial in the middle of a debt-funded capex supercycle. The valuation is deliberately terminal-heavy: the first three forecast years carry ~9% capex against ~4.5% D&A, so near-term owner FCF is near zero and the value rests on capex normalising to 5.5% and the EBITDA margin holding ~13% from year 4. No SBC (J-GAAP), so house and street coincide. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, with a single 7.5% JPY WACC across scenarios. The equity bridge deducts leases (treatment A) and NCI once each and adds the ¥102bn cross-shareholding/affiliate portfolio at an 80% haircut, because its income is outside the modelled flows. M&A and future buybacks are excluded and are upside to the flat share count.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex normalisation: if the ~9% capex intensity persists beyond FY2029 (perovskite phase 2, gigawatt ambitions by 2030) the mature FCF margin is 2-3pp lower and the value falls proportionately; the terminal value is ~65-70% of EV
Pre-emptive demand reversal in H2 FY2027 larger than guided, turning the year-1 beat into a FY2028 decline
High Performance Plastics cyclicality (semiconductor/display/auto/aircraft) at or near a cyclical peak; FY2021 showed OP falling ~45% in a downturn
Recurring portfolio-pruning charges (¥23.3bn impairments in FY2026, more implied in FY2027 guidance) that the component build treats as mostly non-cash
Japanese housing demand under rising mortgage rates and a shrinking population; Housing is 41% of sales
Cross-shareholding portfolio marked at an 80% haircut; a 100% or 60% treatment moves the per-share value by about ¥50 either way
WACC: a 1pp move in the JPY discount rate moves base value by roughly 10-12% because the terminal weight is high

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular TSE close); 52-week range 2,248-3,065
data_sources.financials: research/4204.T/Reports/4204.T_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, J-GAAP consolidated, JPY millions, FY2017-H1 FY2027 repo labels); H1 tanshin for the six months to 30 Sept 2026 (4204.T_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) for the balance sheet, share count and revised FY guidance; FY2025 annual tanshin (4204.T_Annual_FY2025.txt) for capex split, lease repayments, taxes paid and D&A
data_sources.qualitative: research/4204.T/Reports/4204.T_Analysis.json (Accelerate 2028 plan, segment mix, guidance history, bull/bear axes)

inputs.share_count_basis: 405,507,285 issued less 1,610,938 treasury at 30 Sept 2026 (H1 tanshin, after cancellation of ~25.0m treasury shares in the half). No dilutive securities: diluted EPS is shown as '-' in the tanshin. Held FLAT per house rule; buybacks (FY2026 ¥36.4bn, nil in H1 FY2027) have shrunk the count ~2%/yr over nine years and are upside to the flat count, not modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings + commercial paper + bonds at 30 Sept 2026: short-term 27,952 + CP 10,000 + bonds 50,000 + long-term 86,944 = 174,896 (lease liabilities excluded here and deducted separately in equity_bridge). Cash and cash equivalents 103,760 (cash and deposits on the balance sheet are 111,233; the 7.5bn difference is time deposits >3 months, left out conservatively). Net debt rose from 28,918 at 31 Mar 2026 as the Accelerate 2028 capex programme (perovskite line, HPP capacity) is being debt-funded.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was ¥2,057m but is NOT stripped: the company is a net borrower (net debt ¥71bn), so the cash pile is not added to EV and there is no double count.
inputs.sbc_source: not disclosed - J-GAAP tanshin and yuho carry no share-based payment line; StockBasedComp is NULL (not zero) in the Metrics CSV. Treated as an SBC-zero market: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position collapses.
inputs.fy0_note: Repo label FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026, which the company calls 'FY2025'. Projection year 1 (FY2027 in repo labels) is the company's FY2026 guidance year ending 31 March 2027.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.0 gives a cost of equity ~7.2%; after-tax cost of debt ~1% on ~15% debt weight gives a mechanical WACC ~6.3%. Rounded UP to 7.5% for a mid-cap diversified industrial with housing and semiconductor/auto cyclicality; this is the only risk charge in the discount rate - cyclicality, Middle East raw-material risk and perovskite execution are priced in the scenario flows and weights, and the same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once). House reference for small keiretsu suppliers is ~9%; Sekisui Chemical is a ¥1tn Prime-market name with a 57% equity ratio and investment-grade bonds, so a lower rate is warranted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities of ¥21,515m at 30 Sept 2026 (current 5,586 + non-current 15,929; finance leases and IFRS-16 overseas subsidiaries under J-GAAP consolidation) are deducted once in equity_bridge. Lease principal repayments (~¥6bn/yr, in financing) are NOT deducted from the flows; ROU depreciation sits inside D&A and the capex path carries lease-asset renewal. J-GAAP operating leases are already expensed in operating profit, so no further adjustment is needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once: flows are fully consolidated and the non-controlling interests book value of ¥30,137m (30 Sept 2026) is deducted in equity_bridge. NCI share of profit is small (~¥1-2bn/yr, 1-3% of profit), so the book deduction is a fair proxy. FY0 tie: EBIT 106,477 x (1-0.31) = ¥73.5bn NOPAT vs ¥75.2bn attributable profit (which netted ¥23.3bn impairments against FX and non-operating gains).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' + owner-fcf-adaptations). Sekisui Chemical is a diversified Japanese materials/housing operating company (Housing 41%, HPP 35%, UIEP 18%, Medical 7%), not a bank, REIT or holdco, so the FCF engine applies. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). ANCHORS: price from Yahoo chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular TSE close, 52-week range 2,248-3,065); balance sheet and share count from the H1 tanshin for the six months to 30 Sept 2026 (filed late Oct 2026). GUIDANCE: FY ending Mar 2027 was revised up in that filing to net sales ¥1,491.0bn (+13.9%), OP ¥123.0bn (+15.5%), ordinary ¥122.0bn, attributable profit ¥76.0bn (unchanged - the extra ¥8bn of OP is absorbed below the line, implying further restructuring/extraordinary losses), EPS ¥188.17, DPS ¥82. Management explicitly expects 'some degree of reversal from the pre-emptive demand seen in the first half' (customers front-running Middle East raw-material disruption). CAPEX SUPERCYCLE: Accelerate 2028 commits ¥400bn capex over FY2027-FY2029 (repo labels), ~¥133bn/yr vs ~¥60bn D&A, so reported FCF is negative in FY2026 (-¥35.3bn) and H1 FY2027 (-¥24.3bn). The component build carries capex at ~9% of revenue for three years then normalises to 5.5% against D&A rising to 5.0%; this is why last_fcf is negative and uninformative as a base. The ¥300bn M&A envelope is NOT modelled (acquired flows would come with their own cash cost). WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer plus housing purchase-and-resale inventory; growth consumes cash, wc_capture_pct is negative (-15% of the revenue change; historical OCF has run ¥10-25bn below net income + D&A). SBC: none disclosed (J-GAAP), see sbc_source; band_position is null by construction. INVESTMENT SECURITIES: ¥102,243m of investment securities (cross-shareholdings at fair value plus equity-method affiliates) earn dividend and equity-method income OUTSIDE operating profit, so under the matching-asset rule they go into the bridge: added at 80% of carrying value (haircut for ~30% tax on unrealised gains and unlisted-stake illiquidity). TERMINAL: cap multiple 15x in base/bull (Gordon at 1% growth / 7.5% WACC is 15.5x so the cap binds marginally; the market pays ~13x mature FCF today), 13x in bear. HORIZON: 10 years because capex and the FCF margin are still normalising through year 6.

bear.narrative: H2 pre-emptive demand reverses harder than guided (year 1 +10%), then FY2028 is flat as the HPP electronics/mobility cycle turns and Middle East raw-material costs can no longer be fully passed through; housing orders keep falling on higher mortgage rates. EBITDA margin compresses to ~11%, the FY2021-FY2023 range. The ¥400bn capex programme is committed regardless, so the perovskite capital earns little, and restructuring/impairment charges recur. Lower cap (13x) and 0.5% terminal growth reflect a slower, more Japan-bound business.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 at 12.5% is a modest haircut to the revised +13.9% guidance because the implied H2 (+16%) must absorb the pre-emptive-demand reversal management itself flags. Years 2-3 at 4.0/3.5% take FY2029 revenue to ~¥1,585bn, just under the Accelerate 2028 ¥1,600bn target without crediting the M&A envelope. Fades to 1.5% by year 8 (Japan ~68% of sales, shrinking new-build market, offset by renovation, infrastructure renewal and overseas HPP).
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA margin 12.5% (OP 8.1% + D&A 4.3%); H1 FY2027 run-rate 12.7%; revised guidance implies ~12.2% on a higher D&A base. Base matures at 13.0% (OP ~8.0% after D&A rises to 5%), below the Accelerate 2028 9.4% OP-margin target, on the view that spreads normalise as raw-material pass-through unwinds and that ~¥10-20bn/yr of restructuring/impairment leakage has recurred for three years.
base.capex_rationale: ¥400bn three-year capex plan = ~¥133bn/yr (~9% of revenue) FY2027-FY2029, versus FY2026 actual ¥113.6bn (8.7%) and H1 FY2027 ¥59.4bn. Normalises to 5.5% from year 6, ~1pp above the historical gap over D&A, as the perovskite line and HPP capacity complete. D&A rises from 4.3% to 5.0% as the new assets depreciate.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid: FY2024 ¥27.7bn, FY2025 ¥41.9bn, FY2026 ¥35.9bn against pre-tax profit of ¥90-110bn, i.e. 26-38% with timing noise; Japanese statutory ~30.6%. 31% flat.

bull.narrative: Guidance met in full in year 1 and Accelerate 2028 delivered: ¥1,600bn+ sales by FY2029 with the 9.4% OP-margin target (EBITDA 14.2% once D&A reaches 5%). Requires the semiconductor/display upcycle to hold, head-up-display interlayer and aircraft demand to keep compounding, housing mix-shift and renovation to keep offsetting unit declines, and the SOLAFIL perovskite line to ramp on schedule.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because H1's +33% OP growth was partly pre-emptive demand that management itself expects to reverse, HPP (35% of sales) is at a cyclical high in semiconductors/displays, and the ¥400bn capex programme plus ¥300bn M&A envelope is committed before the returns are proven. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (plan margin delivery, the HPP cycle holding, perovskite scaling, housing mix-shift continuing). Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
